_readme: BLIND PROBE v2 — the integrity check on the NLP benchmark.
benchmark.json has a dev split (tuned on) and heldout splits (written as tests).
A held-out split stops being held out the moment someone develops against it.
Probe v1 (evals/blind_probe_v1_burned.json) proved that twice: it scored 50%
exact-triple on the parser whose tuned split read 100% — and then v1 itself was
BURNED on 2026-08-17, when its failure categories were studied and general fixes
landed; its post-study re-score (80%) is a 'were these sentences fixed' number,
not a generalization number, and must never be quoted as blind.
v2 was authored 2026-08-30, AFTER all parser development to date, with the same
adversarial category mix as v1. Authorship disclosure: written by the team's
tooling assistant, which knows the parser's design; cases were written from
office speech, gold labels committed BEFORE any measurement, and the parser was
run against them exactly once per mode. No case here has informed any fix.
RULES OF USE (now enforced by run_blind_probe.py via the 'burned' flag):
1. Never fix a parser bug BY LOOKING AT A CASE IN THIS FILE. Fix the general
rule elsewhere, then re-measure here.
2. The moment failures from this file are studied to inform fixes, set
"burned": true below, archive the file, and author v3.
3. Quote THIS file's single-shot number publicly, never the tuned split.
Gold format matches benchmark.json so the same scorer logic applies.
